title: Dedicated reservoir hedging and adaptive autoscale experiment slate
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: prototype and validate a reservoir-based hedging model for Dedicated pools to allow predictable reserved commitments while enabling burst efficiency via adaptive autoscale. The initiative targets Q3 billing and capacity planning cadence: reduce committed capacity cost by 12–18% for pilot customers while maintaining P95 latency SLOs and <1% request-level fallback to hosted tiers.

Scope:
- Design hedged reservation windows (rolling 6h reservoir + configurable fastpath for 20% burst coverage).
- Implement autoscale policy primitives: reservoir allocation, refill logic, per-customer throttle and backpressure signals, and fallbacks to compatible model variants.
- Trial pricing experiment: introduce a "reservoir credit" SKU that customers can buy monthly to unlock burst above reservation at reduced marginal price.
- Observability: extend Console telemetry to show reservoir utilization, fill-rate, burst frequency, and cost delta per-route.

Success metrics (OKRs / targets):
- O1: Reduce median monthly committed GPU-hours for pilot customers by 15% (Objective metric).
- KR1: Pilot cohort (n=12) shows <1.5x variance in monthly cost vs baseline (budget predictability).
- KR2: Maintain P95 inference latency within 10% of baseline for 99% of requests during burst windows.
- KR3: Fallback rate to hosted (or lower tier model) <= 1% of requests in pilot.

Milestones / Roadmap (high-level):
- Phase A (Sim & ruleset design) — Feb 1 to Mar 15: run historical workload sims against the hedging model, tune refill and retention heuristics. Deliverable: simulation report + policy config set.
- Phase B (Canary prototype) — Mar 16 to Apr 30: enable reservoir policy for 3 pilot customers behind feature flag, add console telemetry and billing metering. Deliverable: canary runbook + live dashboards.
- Phase C (Pricing pilot + widen) — May 1 to Jun 30: expose reservoir credit SKU to pilot customers, monitor economic impact and acceptance. Deliverable: pricing experiment results and recommended SKU.
- Phase D (Rollout / docs) — Jul 1 to Aug 15: documentation, SDK knobs, and GA readiness checklist.

Key design decisions & trade-offs: 
- Hedged reservoirs vs larger reserved pools: reservoirs enable lower committed spend and better utilization but add complexity in billing/observability and edge-case latency regressions under correlated bursts. We accept controlled small-percent fallbacks to preserve overall economics.
- Fallback policy: prefer routing to a quantized/cheaper model variant within the same region before routing to hosted (cross-region) to minimize latency impact.
- Pricing model: reservoir-credit is additive rather than replacing reservations to keep existing committed customers' billing predictable.

Telemetry & alerting requirements:
- New console panels: reservoir-utilization-per-pool, burst-frequency, per-customer refill-rate, cost-delta-per-1M-tokens.
- Alerts: reservoir-depletion-rate > 60% sustained for 10m; fallback-rate > 0.5% rolling 1h for pilot customers.

Rollout playbook (canary):
1) Confirm infra readiness: autoscale primitives implemented in Dedicated control plane (ENG owner: Lina Chen).
2) Run 48h synthetic stress tests mirroring pilot customer profiles.
3) Enable feature flag for 3 pilot customers (low-risk, high-traffic).
4) Monitor telemetry for 72h, run post-mortem if fallback_rate > 1% or P95 latency exceeds threshold.
5) Iterate policy parameters and re-run.

Artifacts & links:
- Simulation notebook + data: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/reservoir-sims-q1-2026
- Runbook draft (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DED/Reservoir+Hedging+Runbook
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DED/Reservoir-Design-v1.0
- Initial implementation PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2941, https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/881
- Dashboard (prototype): https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/reservoir-pilot

Open risks & mitigation: 
- Risk: Correlated bursts across multiple customers could exhaust shared burst capacity. Mitigation: enforce per-customer caps, progressive degradation, and automated throttles with customer notification.
- Risk: Billing/finance complexity with hybrid SKU. Mitigation: finance to run modeled invoices for pilot cohort and sign off on SKU structure before public rollout. (Dependency: FIN-approval)
- Risk: SRE operational load responding to unanticipated fallback storms. Mitigation: create automated playbooks and escalation paths; train on-call for Phase B.

Acceptance criteria for Phase B canary:
- Console telemetry shows stable reservoir utilization and refill behavior consistent with sims.
- No customer-experienced P95 regression > 10% during a 7-day rolling window.
- Engineering team signs off on rollback path and throttles.
